doc.title: Howie Shear interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2014

title: Favorite film composers
summary: Shear names Max Steiner, Bernard Herrmann, Jerry Goldsmith and Korngold as favorites.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: Who are your favorite film scorer people?

Oh gosh, well Max Steiner from the early days of film was one of the greats. I think Bernard Herrmann, who did Psycho, the movie Psycho. And he really changed the way, especially strings are scored in films. And Bernard Herrmann, he did a lot of the “Twilight Zones” early on. And then he did many of the Hitchcock films. I think he died in 1974 I believe. I think Taxi Driver was his last film. But he also did the original Cape Fear back in the 40s and the score was so great to that that when they redid it with DeNiro they kept the score, they just reworked it.

Yeah, they said it can’t be better than that. We can’t get anybody to — so I think Bernard Herrmann is my favorite; and Jerry Goldsmith, who passed away a few years ago, who studied with Bernard Herrmann, he’s one of my favorite scorers. So those three come to mind right away. And then there’s Korngold of course, from the older school.
Korngold yeah. He’s a European composer also. He was known as a swashbuckling composer because he did all those pirate movies, like the original Robin Hood.
